To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diffusion of a fast diffuser under the influence of a thermal gradient driving force can be approximated by a parabolic diffusion profile, that the concentration profile is independent of the magnitude of the thermal gradient, that the diffusion profile can be approximated as a parabolic profile, that the diffusion of fast diffusers in a gradient is not a function of the thermal gradient and that the diffusion of Ni in Sn can be approximated using Fick's first law of diffusion.

(i) a thermal gradient driving force is a major factor in determining the reliability of lead-free solder joints, (ii) the effect of a thermal gradient is to increase the concentration of the fast diffuser at the interface, (iii) the effect is more pronounced for a fast diffusing element, such as Ni, and (iv) the effect is greater for larger thermal gradients
the diffusion of Ni in Sn can be described by the following equation: D = 1.3 10-14exp(-0.8eV/kT).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fast diffuser in the thermal gradient is not a problem for the reliability of solder joints.
fast diffusers in a gradient are a potential reliability problem.
the fast diffuser in a thermal gradient driving force is not expected to have any significant effect on the reliability of the solder joint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fast diffuser in a gradient is not a fast diffuser.
the concentration profile for a fast diffusing species is not a straight line, but a concave curve, with a minimum concentration at the interface between the two phases.
the fast diffuser in the solder is a potential reliability issue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concentration profiles of a fast diffuser in a thermal gradient can be very different from the concentration profiles of the same element in an isothermal system.
the concentration profiles are very sensitive to the thermal gradient and to the diffusivity ratio between the two elements.
the fast diffusion of Ni in Sn in the presence of a thermal gradient is a significant reliability issue that must be addressed.
